name: Mitski
label: Dead Oceans
lede: Mitski grew up in 13 countries, studied at Purchase College and, eight albums in, writes the songs people quote back to themselves.

eras.title: Thirteen countries, no hometown
eras.text: Born in Japan and raised on the move by a father in the US State Department, Mitski Miyawaki lands in New York in 2010 and finally stays put. The piano comes with her.

years.h: Mitsuki Laycock is born in Mie Prefecture, Japan
years.p: She'll take her mother's surname, Miyawaki. Her father's State Department work moves the family through 13 countries before she's out of school.
years.xp:
Wikipedia describes her as a "third culture kid": she arrives in the US at 15, does high school in Alabama and Virginia, and graduates early from Ankara, Turkey.

That itinerary is the backdrop to nearly everything she writes about belonging.

years.h: Hunter College film, then the Purchase conservatory
years.p: She lands in New York in 2010, starts in film at Hunter, then transfers to Purchase's Conservatory of Music, where she meets [[Patrick Hyland|6e58e75a-b1b9-40bc-b227-59a3c4659eee]].
years.xp: She studies studio composition and earns a Bachelor of Music in 2013. Hyland goes on to produce every album she makes after Lush, per Wikipedia.

eras.title: Homework turns into a career
eras.text: The first two albums are class projects posted to Bandcamp. The third, with guitars up front and a real label, is the one strangers start writing about.

years.h: Lush goes up on Bandcamp as a junior-year project
years.p: Scot Moriarty records and mixes it. It's chamber pop built around piano, with lo-fi and punk edges.
years.xp:
The tracklist changed after release: "Real Men" came off Bandcamp in late 2012 or early 2013, and in July 2022 streaming services were updated to match the shorter Bandcamp version (8 tracks, 23:15).

Mitski has described the record's author as a version of herself that is "long gone now."

years.h: A 60-person student orchestra backs her senior project
years.p: Retired from Sad, New Career in Business goes on Bandcamp August 1, 2013, and she graduates from Purchase the same year.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists it as a self-released senior-project collaboration with a student orchestra. It's the last record she makes as a student and the last before guitars take over.

years.src: Wikipedia: Bury Me at Makeout Creek
years.h: Guitars arrive on Bury Me at Makeout Creek
years.p: It's her first release on Double Double Whammy, produced by Hyland. Pitchfork's Ian Cohen scores it 7.7 and calls it "a breakthrough."
years.xp:
Wikipedia says she learned guitar and recorded in makeshift studios while juggling school, side jobs and music, and that the exhaustion shaped the record's tone. The title comes from The Simpsons. Stereogum later called it a turning point that let her let out her rage.

Singles "First Love / Late Spring" (May), "Townie" (September), "I Don't Smoke" and "I Will" (October) came before release.

eras.title: A new label and a Colbert booking
eras.text: A reissue, a new label and a fourth album about not fitting in. By the end of 2016 Mitski is on late-night television.

years.src: Wikipedia: Bury Me at Makeout Creek
years.h: Don Giovanni reissues Bury Me with four live tracks
years.p: The New Jersey label adds four live bonus tracks to the Double Double Whammy original.

years.h: Mitski signs with Dead Oceans
years.p: The Bloomington label, part of the Secretly Group alongside Secretly Canadian and Jagjaguwar, becomes her home for every album from Puberty 2 on.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Dead Oceans was founded on June 30, 2006 by Phil Waldorf and Chris Swanson. Its Mitski catalogue runs from Puberty 2 (2016) through Nothing's About to Happen to Me (2026).

years.h: Zia Anger films "Your Best American Girl"
years.p: Mitski says the video plays on being a Japanese girl who never quite fits with indie rock's supply of white American guys.
years.xp:
The video lands April 13, 2016 and nods to PJ Harvey's look. Critics heard Weezer's Pinkerton and Pixies guitars in the song, which leads off Puberty 2.

Per Wikipedia, Pitchfork ranked it 16th on its 100 best songs of 2016 and NPR put it second on its 2016 list.

years.cap: Mitski at Paradise Rock Club, Boston, November 1, 2016
yt: Your Best American Girl, live for World Cafe
years.h: Two weeks at Acme Studios, then Puberty 2
years.p: Hyland produces it in Westchester County, New York. Pitchfork gives it 8.5; Time puts it third on its year's list.
years.xp:
Pitchfork's Jillian Mapes heard "second-wave emo," dream pop, electronics, folk-punk and '60s pop hooks in it. NPR's Laura Snapes called it "a strike against the happy/sad poles that govern our lives."

Wikipedia counts it in the top ten of several publications' 2016 lists, among them The A.V. Club, Paste, Stereogum and Time.

years.h: Colbert gives her network TV debut
years.p: She plays "Your Best American Girl" on The Late Show with Stephen Colbert.

eras.title: One spotlight, no crowd
eras.text: Be the Cowboy is built around one image: a person alone on a stage in a dark room. It's also the record that makes her impossible to file under "indie singer-songwriter."

years.cap: Mitski on the Be the Cowboy tour, October 31, 2018
years.h: "Nobody" starts on a toy piano in Kuala Lumpur
years.p: Mitski wrote it over Christmas in Malaysia, alone in a country where she knew no one. The video took five days to shoot in Kansas City.
years.xp:
She told the story of the toy piano, bought at Toys "R" Us, and of the holidays: "I was completely, unexpectedly crushed by the fact that I not only didn't know anyone in the country."

The video's choreography and camera angles were locked down shot by shot, including a magnifying-glass moment.

years.cap: Mitski on the Be the Cowboy tour, October 31, 2018
years.src: Wikipedia: Be the Cowboy · Wikipedia: Mitski
years.h: At 32 minutes, Be the Cowboy tops Pitchfork's year
years.p: Pitchfork's Quinn Moreland calls it "Mitski's greatest to date," scores it 8.8, and Pitchfork ranks it its best album of 2018. Consequence does the same.
years.xp:
Hyland produced across studios in Philadelphia, Haddon Heights and Los Angeles. Mitski said she was after "the image of someone alone on a stage, singing solo with a single spotlight trained on them in an otherwise dark room."

It's her first Billboard 200 entry, at No. 52, and was nominated for a Grammy for Best Recording Package.

years.h: "Washing Machine Heart" almost misses the album
years.p: Hyland told BBC 6 Music the two-minute song wasn't originally going to be on Be the Cowboy. Zia Anger's black-and-white video lands November 1.
years.xp: Rolling Stone noted that it runs two minutes but holds at least three distinct musical ideas. The A.V. Club called it a "deranged domestic ballad." It was never an official single but charted at No. 26 on the UK Indie chart.

eras.title: Last show indefinitely
eras.text: Five years of near-constant touring end in Central Park. Mitski moves to Nashville, disappears from social media, and is dragged back into the conversation when TikTok finds "Nobody."

years.cap: Mitski at Capitol Hill Block Party, Seattle, July 19, 2019
q: It's time to be a human again.
years.src: The Nation · Wikipedia: Working for the Knife · Wikipedia: Mitski
years.h: "Last show indefinitely" at SummerStage
years.p: Mitski tells the Central Park crowd it's her last show for now. Her social accounts are run by staff from here.
years.xp:
Her hiatus statement said she sensed her "self-worth/identity will start depending too much on staying in the game." Fans read it as a retirement; she clarified she wasn't leaving music entirely. Per Wikipedia she later told Rolling Stone she had intended to quit the music industry.

Sources give the date as September 7 or 9.

years.h: Mitski settles in Nashville
years.p: Per Wikipedia she moves around 2019, to get away from competitive, expensive cities.

years.h: TikTok finds "Nobody" three years late
years.p: Users film themselves running from the camera to the song's crescendo. By February 2022 her music sits under more than 2.5 million TikTok videos.
years.xp: The Nation reports her daily streaming numbers multiplied sevenfold. The song later went platinum in the US.

years.h: Mitski comes back with "Working for the Knife"
years.p: Her first release since Be the Cowboy. That's how touring felt, she told Rolling Stone, as The Nation reports it.
years.xp:
Her 2019 hiatus statement had worried about self-worth depending on staying in "the constant churn."

Zia Anger's video was shot at The Egg in Albany, New York: Mitski in a black leather trench and cowboy hat, then a modern-dance routine that ends in a butoh-inspired collapse, first to simulated applause, then to none.

Rolling Stone's Angie Martoccio compared the song to "Blue Light" from Be the Cowboy.

eras.title: Back on synths
eras.text: She comes back on synths with a top-five album, to an audience TikTok built while she was away.

years.cap: Mitski at Day In Day Out Festival, Seattle, August 12, 2022
years.h: Laurel Hell debuts at No. 5 on the Billboard 200
years.p: Hyland produces the synth-pop, and it's Dead Oceans' first Billboard 200 top ten. Pitchfork gives it 7.8.
years.xp:
Mitski says the title is a folk term for being trapped in the thickets of laurel that grow in the southern Appalachians. She wrote most of it around 2018 and finished it during COVID lockdowns.

Per Wikipedia it was the best-selling album in the US its release week and No. 1 on the Top Alternative and Top Rock albums charts; Metacritic scores it 83.

years.h: "The Only Heartbreaker" reaches No. 1 on Adult Alternative Airplay
years.p: Barack Obama had already put it on his list of favorite songs of 2021.

years.h: Mitski plays Glastonbury
years.p: It falls in the middle of the Laurel Hell tour, which runs February to November 2022 across North America and Europe.

eras.title: An orchestra and a choir
eras.text: An orchestra, a choir, a pedal steel and a Nashville studio: her most American record, and the one that gets her onto the Hot 100.

years.h: An Oscar nomination for "This Is a Life"
years.p: She co-writes it with Son Lux for Everything Everywhere All at Once, and it's up for Best Original Song.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists David Byrne as a co-writer alongside Son Lux.

years.h: "Bug Like an Angel" announces a new album
years.p: The lead single arrives with a video directed by Noel Paul and the news that a new record is coming September 15 on Dead Oceans.
years.xp: Exclaim! lists producer Patrick Hyland, orchestra arranged and conducted by [[Drew Erickson|e5dd9859-5d60-4ecc-ab05-6da4cc9bb5ef]], and a choir of 17 arranged by Mitski.

years.cap: Mitski at Union Chapel, London, October 11, 2023
years.src: Wikipedia: The Land Is Inhospitable and So Are We · Album of the Year · Exclaim!
years.h: A 17-voice choir and an orchestra back The Land Is Inhospitable and So Are We
years.p: It's recorded at Bomb Shelter in Nashville and Sunset Sound in Los Angeles. Pitchfork gives it 8.1 and ranks it No. 23 of 2023.
years.xp:
Erickson's orchestra and the choir (12 voices in LA, 5 in Nashville) play on it, and Exclaim! says it was the first time she recorded with a full band in the studio. Mitski has called it her "most American album," citing spaghetti Westerns, Arthur Russell and Stravinsky.

Metacritic scores it 90. Rolling Stone ranked it No. 7 of 2023, Paste No. 8, Exclaim! No. 2. It peaked at No. 12 on the Billboard 200 and No. 4 in the UK.
play: The Land Is Inhospitable and So Are We

years.cap: Mitski at the Moda Center, Portland, September 21, 2024
years.src: Wikipedia: My Love Mine All Mine
yt: My Love Mine All Mine (official video)
years.h: "My Love Mine All Mine" becomes her first Hot 100 hit
years.p: It debuts at No. 76 on the chart dated September 30, 2023 and peaks at No. 26. The video has Mitski stacking dining chairs on an egg.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia it passed 1 billion Spotify streams by July 2024, and TikTok went from 300,000 videos in October 2023 to 2.2 million by July 2024. Critics tagged it goth-country; Obama named it a 2023 favorite; Clairo posted a cover.

years.h: Listening parties come with Days of Heaven and La Strada
years.p: Mitski announces cinema events pairing album listens with screenings of Days of Heaven, Desert Hearts, Drugstore Cowboy and La Strada.

eras.title: Three nights at the Fox, then a new record
eras.text: The Land tour gets filmed in Atlanta and released as a movie and a live album. In 2026 she's back with an eighth album.

years.h: Three nights at Atlanta's Fox Theatre get filmed
years.p: A seven-piece band, including Patrick Hyland, plays songs from the 2023 album and reworked older ones.
years.xp: Grant James directed. Choreography is by Monica Mirabile, stage design by Andi Watson.

years.h: Mitski: The Land hits 630 theaters, and a live album follows
years.p: The 78-minute film opens October 22 in 30 countries. The Land: The Live Album (21 songs) surprise-drops on Bandcamp October 16.

years.src: Wikipedia: Nothing's About to Happen to Me
years.h: Her eighth album, Nothing's About to Happen to Me
years.p: Dead Oceans again, produced by Hyland at Sunset Sound and TTG in Los Angeles. It reaches No. 10 on the Billboard 200; Pitchfork gives it 7.7.
years.xp: The Guardian's Alexis Petridis and NME's Joe Goggins each gave it five stars; Consequence gave it a B+. Metacritic scores it 87. Residencies in New York, Los Angeles and Sydney were announced February 3.
play: Nothing's About to Happen to Me
